title: In this town, the little flame over your head always leans toward home
premise: In a lake town, a small amber flame floats over every head and always leans toward home. Mine never leans toward my flat. Each Saturday I visit Grandad's red fishing hut on the frozen lake, and each time the fog lifts a rust-red person with no flame stands a little nearer, tipped at a slant no one could hold.
twist: My flame was never wandering: it leans toward home, and home is Grandad. It followed him around town, in the car and across the ice, and the thing on the ice stood where the second stool's empty seat was.
world: a frozen lake with painted wooden fishing huts and low gold sun, fog rolling in and lifting, a small town on the shore, a red hut with two stools over one hole
